title: Stop Secret Spending Act of 2025
official_title: To amend the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006 to ensure that other transaction agreements are reported to USAspending.gov, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Barry Moore (R-AL-1) with three cosponsors, including Rep. Panetta (D-CA) and Rep. Goodlander (D-NH), a cross-party mix. The bill adds disclosure requirements to an existing transparency database without appropriating any funds — a low-cost good-government subject with broad bipartisan appeal. The main friction comes from agencies and recipients that rely on other transaction agreements to contract quickly, but the multi-year phase-in and the report's carve-outs for classified and national-security spending narrow that opposition.

referencedSources.label: 31 U.S.C. 6101 (Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act note)

summary: USAspending.gov is the searchable public website created by the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006 (FFATA), where Federal agencies post data on Federal awards such as grants and contracts. This bill adds "other transaction agreements" to FFATA's definition of a covered Federal award and requires the Secretary of the Treasury to ensure that, within 3 years of enactment, OTA data is automatically transmitted to the website with a centralized view available; it also requires an annual report identifying Federal spending not posted to the site and the reasons why, and a published list of the Federal agencies required to post information.
brief: Adds "other transaction agreements" to the awards Federal agencies must report on USAspending.gov and requires that data to flow to the site within 3 years of enactment.

items.main: Expands the FFATA definition of covered "Federal award" to include other transaction agreements, and directs the Secretary of the Treasury to ensure OTA data is automatically transmitted to USAspending.gov within 3 years of enactment with a centralized view of the data.
items.detail: Amends section 2(a)(4)(A) of the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006 (31 U.S.C. 6101 note) to add "(iii) includes other transaction agreements" plus technical cross-reference fixes in paragraph (7). Amends section 4 to require the Secretary to ensure that, within 3 years of enactment, OTA data is automatically transmitted to the website established under FFATA section 2 (or any successor website) and that a centralized view of the data is available.

items.main: Requires the Secretary of the Treasury (in consultation with the OMB Director) to post an annual report to USAspending.gov identifying total Federal spending on awards not posted and the reasons why.
items.detail: Adds a new FFATA subsection (h) requiring, within 1 year of enactment and annually thereafter, a report listing the total amount of Federal spending on Federal awards for which data has not been posted and the reason it has not been posted — including whether the spending was national-security-related or classified, awarded or entered into by a legislative or judicial branch agency, or a subaward below a primary subaward.

items.main: Adds a two-step implementation plan requiring an initial detailed OTA compilation within 1 year and a plan to Congress within 2 years if OTA data is not yet flowing to USAspending.gov.
items.detail: If the Secretary has not complied with the new OTA subsection (e) by the 1-year mark, the Secretary must publish on USAspending.gov a report listing and describing in detail all OTAs entered into by relevant agencies for the preceding fiscal year. If not complied with by the 2-year mark, the Secretary must submit to Congress a plan describing the status and the actions underway and planned to fully incorporate OTA data by the 3-year mark.

items.main: Restructures FFATA Inspector General reporting to run from the agencies described in paragraphs (1) and (2) of 31 U.S.C. 901(b), on a schedule tied to enactment.
items.detail: Strikes the prior FFATA paragraph (2) and inserts a new one requiring the inspector general of each covered agency to submit to Congress and make publicly available an initial report within 1 year of enactment and not less than once every 2 years thereafter, until 10 years after enactment, on the date of submission of the report required under 31 U.S.C. 3521(f) or 9105(a)(3).

items.main: Requires the Secretary of the Treasury and OMB to establish quality-of-information requirements, verify accuracy, and publish a list of the Federal agencies and components required to post information under FFATA.
items.detail: Adds new FFATA subsections (c) through (e). Subsection (c) requires the Secretary and the Director, in consultation with agency heads, to establish requirements for complete and accurate information, makes agency heads responsible for accuracy, and gives the Secretary and Director authority to verify posted data. Subsection (d) requires agencies to comply with display standards. Subsection (e) requires the Secretary, in coordination with the Director, to determine within 1 year of enactment (and at least every 2 years thereafter) which Federal agencies and components must post information, publish the list on the FFATA website, and notify each covered agency head and inspector general.

items.main: Directs the Comptroller General to make, within 1 year of enactment, recommendations for updates to clause 52.204.10 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation that incorporate FFATA reporting requirements.
items.detail: The Comptroller General shall make recommendations for any updates the Comptroller General determines advisable to clause 52.204.10 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation with respect to incorporating requirements under the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006 (31 U.S.C. 6101 note).

underreported.section: Section 3(b) — Full Disclosure of Federal Funds
underreported.summary: The bill scopes FFATA reporting to agencies and components identified on a list the Secretary must publish, with the amendments to the underlying disclosure rules taking effect only when the first list is published.
underreported.why_unreported: The section heading reads "Full Disclosure of Federal Funds" but the mechanical effect narrows the immediate universe of covered posters to those on the published list — an agency not yet on the list does not have the new complete-and-accurate posting obligations.

underreported.summary: The Inspector General reporting requirement runs until the date that is 10 years after the date of enactment.
underreported.why_unreported: Section 3 is captioned "Other Amendments" but embedded in the IG paragraph is a 10-year time limit on the recurring IG report that is not signaled by the section heading.

gaps: The bill mandates OTA data flow to USAspending.gov but does not define "other transaction agreement" or specify which OTA-issuing agencies must comply beyond "a Federal agency ... that has the authority to enter into an other transaction agreement, as determined by the Director" of OMB.

The bill requires an annual report on unreported Federal spending with three exception categories (national-security or classified, legislative or judicial branch, sub-awards) but does not require any breakdown by dollar amount within those categories.
The bill requires agency IG reports at least every 2 years for 10 years but does not identify a lead agency to consolidate the reports or synthesize government-wide findings.
The bill requires the Secretary to publish a list of covered agencies but does not set a process for an agency (or the public) to appeal inclusion in or exclusion from the list.
The bill directs the Comptroller General to recommend updates to FAR clause 52.204.10 but does not require that the recommendations be adopted or set a deadline for acting on them.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Ernst
featured_quotes.text: Taxpayers deserve to know how the money they send to Washington is being spent. For 20 years now, the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act has required unclassified government spending to be put online in a searchable public website, USAspending.gov. This allows taxpayers to review the receipts for themselves.

added: New FFATA section 2(a)(4)(A)(iii) — "includes other transaction agreements" added to the definition of a Federal award
New FFATA subsection 4(e) — Treasury must ensure OTA data is automatically transmitted to USAspending.gov and a centralized view is available
New FFATA subsection 2(h) — annual report on total Federal spending not posted, with reasons
New FFATA subsection 3(c) — Treasury and OMB requirements for complete and accurate posted information
New FFATA subsection 3(d) — Treasury display standards for posted information
New FFATA subsection 3(e) — Treasury agency reporting determination and published list of covered agencies
New two-step implementation plan (initial OTA compilation at 1 year, plan to Congress at 2 years) tied to the 3-year OTA-transmission deadline
New GAO study within 1 year on updates to FAR clause 52.204.10
modified: FFATA section 6(a) (Inspector General reports) — scope narrowed from "each Federal agency" to agencies described in paragraphs (1) and (2) of 31 U.S.C. 901(b); IG reports required within 1 year of enactment and not less than every 2 years until 10 years after enactment
FFATA section 3(b) — posting duty tied to agencies and components on the published list
removed: Prior FFATA section 6(a)(2) — replaced with a new deadline structure tied to enactment of this Act
